summary: This clipped web page is the landing page of the Synesthesia Battery, an online standardized test battery for detecting and studying synesthesia. It explains what synesthesia is, how the battery works for synesthetes and researchers, and how to cite the battery's published validation papers. It also mentions a companion book and translations of the battery.
one_line: Landing page for the Synesthesia Battery, an online standardized test suite for studying and detecting synesthesia.
key_facts: Synesthesia (British spelling synaesthesia) is a rare trait that gives rise to a type of 'merging of sensations'.
Some synaesthetes see colours when they hear music, and for others colours might attach to letters, numbers or words, e.g., A might be red and Monday might be green.
The Synesthesia Battery provides a standard battery of questions, tests and scoring for the whole community of researchers and synesthetes.
Data entered into the Synesthesia Battery is kept entirely private, for use only by the synesthete and by a researcher if a valid email address is provided for one.
Users unsure whether they are synesthetes can answer a few preview questions to find out.
After completing the questionnaire, synesthetes are automatically routed to the online software tests appropriate for the forms of synesthesia they experience.
Researchers can direct synesthetic subjects to the site and ask them to include the researcher's email address when registering.
The standardized scoring system allows data combination or comparison among laboratories.

The battery is cited as David M. Eagleman, Arielle D. Kagan, Stephanie S. Nelson, Deepak Sagaram, Anand K. Sarma, 'A standardized test battery for the study of Synesthesia', Journal of Neuroscience Methods, 2007 Jan 15;159(1):139-145.
A 2015 validation paper by Carmichael, D A, Down, M P, Shillcock, R C, Eagleman, D M and Simner, J is published in Consciousness and Cognition, 33, pp. 375-385.
The 2015 paper's title asks whether the Synesthesia Battery reliably detects synesthesia.
The companion book is titled Wednesday Is Indigo Blue: Discovering the Brain of Synesthesia.
The site offers language options: english, german, chinese, french, czech, turkish, greek and ukrainian.
The Ukrainian translation was sponsored by the International Association of Synaesthetes, Artists, and Scientists (IASAS), translated by Eugenia Slovachevska and curated by Anton Sidoroff-Dorso.
The site copyright is listed as 2005-2024 David Eagleman.
